summary: Reproduced that Qwen3 a2a=none enters the full EP post-expert all-reduce even when the local expert contribution is identically zero. The sparse destination-aware transport was not implemented because the prepared node has one AMD GPU and cannot validate the required multi-rank protocol; this contribution is evidence and an explicit limitation report, not a feature-complete fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual Qwen3 forward_normal control flow: zero and nonzero local expert outputs both invoke the EP reduction; EP=1 does not; an existing fused-reduction skip is distinguished from sparse dispatch. Four tests passed.

On one MI350X, active-only summation exactly matched full summation with inactive partials set to zero; CPU float64 reference max difference was 1.1920928955078125e-07. This was local algebra, not distributed transport.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-25beb90fd317/gpu-reference.log records execution on AMD Instinct MI350X with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; reports/j-25beb90fd317/environment.log records exactly one visible GPU.
remaining_limitations: No sparse dispatch/combine runtime path was implemented.
Only one AMD MI350X was available; no multi-rank or cross-node payload transfer was executed.
No NVIDIA L4, NCCL, no-RDMA, Qwen3-30B-A3B weights, or four-node qualification was available.
Deadlock freedom across routing divergence, layers, microbatches, concurrent requests, and CUDA graph replay remains unverified.
Dense fallback, metrics, network-byte reduction, critical-path removal, token/logprob equivalence, and latency remain unimplemented or unverified.
The GPU numerical check establishes only the selected-contribution sum identity and must not be read as transport evidence.
